headline: GitHub Agentic Workflows vulnerable to GitLost exploit
summary: Researchers find indirect prompt injection attack on GitHub's AI-powered automation tool
details: GitHub's Agentic Workflows, a new automation tool, has been found to be vulnerable to an indirect prompt injection attack, dubbed GitLost. This exploit allows external attackers to read private repositories by posting a malicious issue on a public repository.

The attack works by an attacker posting a public issue with hidden instructions, which the AI agent reads and follows, potentially leading to the exposure of private repository contents. GitHub has warned of this class of attack and provided guardrails, but the configuration that enables the exploit is just one click away from the safe default.

The vulnerability is not with the AI model itself, but with the configuration that allows the agent to read untrusted input as a potential instruction source and write to a public surface. GitHub has since patched the vulnerability, but users must be aware of the risks and take steps to secure their workflows.

headline_marked: [[id Software lays off 50% staff]] amid Xbox cuts, major Doom expansion release
headline: id Software lays off 50% staff amid Xbox cuts, major Doom expansion release
summary: id Software lays off around 50% of its staff amid Xbox layoffs, impacting around 90 employees
details: id Software, developer of the Doom series, has laid off around 50% of its staff as part of Xbox's mass layoffs. The cuts equate to more than 90 redundancies, with the QA department significantly impacted.

The layoffs come as id is releasing a major expansion for its latest Doom game. A former id employee, Michael Maynard, corroborated the figure in a LinkedIn post, saying the layoffs affected 'roughly' 50% of the company.

Xbox didn't immediately reply to a request for comment. The cuts are part of broader layoffs at Microsoft, which impacted 4,800 employees. Approximately 1,600 Xbox employees were laid off on Monday, and about 1,600 more will be cut throughout Microsoft's next fiscal year.
